claims.text: The target HfNbTaTiZr contains inherent atomic-scale disorder.
The target sample contains approximately 1 wt.% oxygen.
The proposed framework will explicitly compute anharmonic phonon spectra.
The proposed phonon calculations will incorporate impurity scattering.
The proposed framework will calculate electronic transport using Green's-function, many-body, or Boltzmann methods.
Explicit treatment of disorder and impurities will permit separate prediction of lattice and electronic heat transport.
Physics-specific treatment of phonons and electrons will capture temperature-dependent scattering processes and impurity effects.
Previous methods averaged out or neglected temperature-dependent scattering and impurity effects.
Previous Debye-based or averaged DFT approaches conflated lattice and electronic thermal-conductivity contributions.
Previous methods neglected impurity and disorder effects.
Below 200 K, lattice and electronic heat-transport contributions in HfNbTaTiZr are approximately equal.
Between 300 and 1200 K, HfNbTaTiZr containing about 1 wt.% oxygen has a total thermal conductivity of 10–17 W/(K m).
Oxygen scattering significantly affects thermal conductivity between 300 and 1200 K.
The hybrid framework will predict thermal conductivity more accurately than previous Debye-based or averaged DFT approaches.
The hybrid framework will reduce prediction error by approximately 30% relative to prior models.
Separately predicted lattice and electronic contributions will match measured trends more closely than conflated estimates.
The proposed approach is applicable to HfNbTaTiZr with oxygen levels around 1 wt.% at temperatures below 200 K and from 300 to 1200 K.
Outside the stated temperature and impurity ranges, additional defects or extreme conditions may require model adjustments.
Deviation of the separately predicted contributions by more than 30% from independent measurements would falsify the hypothesis.
